thesis: Franco-Nevada is up about 32% over the past 60 calendar days, driven by a broad gold-price rally -- spot gold climbed above $4,350/oz after a disappointing U.S. jobs report cut rate-hike expectations -- rather than any company-specific disclosed event; Franco-Nevada also reported record Q1 2026 results, and its royalty/streaming model lets it capture higher metal prices without absorbing mine-level operating costs. The strongest counter-evidence is that gold has already pulled back 20-25% from its January 2026 all-time high near $5,500/oz, and the stock itself sits roughly 7% below its own 52-week high, so today's continued strength is riding a macro commodity cycle that could reverse as easily as it advanced -- the record Q1 results are real, but the bulk of the last 60 days' move is a gold-price story rather than a newly disclosed company catalyst, and this counter-case is not resolved beyond noting the model's structural leverage to prices staying elevated.
invalidation: A reversal in spot gold prices back toward the low-$3,000s, or evidence Franco-Nevada's own portfolio production/royalty economics are deteriorating independent of the metal price.

thesis: Vertiv fell roughly 8-11% today (Sep 9) and is down about 14% over the past 60 calendar days on a volume surge (2.42x the 30-day average), as investors take profits across AI data-center infrastructure names amid valuation scrutiny -- VRT trades near ~79.7x earnings versus ~40x for the peer group, above analysts' own implied fair-value multiple (~60x). The proximate trigger traces to Vertiv's own Q2 earnings call, where management flagged 'minor timing shifts' in revenue tied to multi-phase project execution and supply-chain congestion -- a real, company-disclosed data point, though one explicitly framed as minor rather than a guidance cut. Sell-side coverage remains broadly bullish (28 analysts: 3 Strong Buy, 21 Buy, 4 Hold, 0 Sell, one shop targeting a roughly 100% rally), but that optimism predates today's drop and doesn't resolve whether the pullback reflects a durable re-rating of an expensive stock or a buyable overreaction -- the setup stays genuinely mixed rather than a clear net read.
invalidation: Evidence the Q2 timing shifts are resolving on schedule with no further guidance slippage, or the stock re-rating to a multiple more in line with peers before a fresh entry is considered.
